signals.evidence: Two people injured in light condition in Kiryat Shmona: 85-year-old with hand injury and 34-year-old with internal injury from rocket fire
Two men aged 30 and 40 injured from shrapnel after rocket impact near school in Ba'ana; several people treated for anxiety

Udai Ayat (32) murdered in Baqa al-Gharbiyeh. Father Subhi Ayat said: 'My son was an only son alongside 10 daughters. He was born to us after 25 years. Yesterday he left the house and said to me, I'll be back soon, and unfortunately he came back without breath of life.'
Father of murdered son Subhi Ayat: 'We are between two wars, we don't know who is next in line'

Mitav, reservist couple: 'Nothing remained, from wallet level to electrical products and furniture. The section where we lived was damaged most severely, and there is no possibility to enter it due to collapse risk. It is 100% loss.'

Mitav: 'I was supposed to be there at the last moment, but I decided to travel north. Without planning, I just took a few things and came. It's a miracle, but it's hard to see it this way when everything disappeared in a second.'
Two toddlers aged seven months injured in light condition in Bnei Brak from rocket fire

Child Hila: 'I was very small... I was in kindergarten. I barely had first grade because Corona started. Corona was something I didn't really understand, but they did explain it to us. It's hard. Every time running to the safe room, hearing the booms, and the sirens and the news. And fear.'
Mother Shirley: 'It matured them quickly. Changed the character, the coping. Not always for the better.'
Two men aged 85 and 34 injured in light condition from shrapnel in Kiryat Shmona after rocket fire from Lebanon
Two men aged 85 and 34 injured in light condition from shrapnel in Kiryat Shmona; property damage at six locations in the city
One person injured in light condition in Mitzpe Rama from interception debris; two men aged 30 and 40 injured in light condition in Ba'ana from shrapnel near school
Two injured in light condition in Petah Tikva and a youth injured in Mitzpe Rama from Iranian missile fire; two men aged 30 and 40 injured from shrapnel in Ba'ana
14 people injured during morning barrages; girl injured severely in Bnei Brak; 23 people injured on way to safe rooms during evening and night barrages
Residents entered protected spaces during Seder night alerts; roads emptied similar to Yom Kippur as residents sheltered
Four people injured in light condition in Bnei Brak: two toddlers aged seven months, one person aged 24, one aged 12, and one woman aged 34 with anxiety

Israel Nahum, resident of Ramat Gan: 'At the beginning of Seder night there were sirens and we were in a shelter. After the Home Front Command announcement that we could leave the protected space, we continued the Seder as required - but remained tense.'

Haim, driver on Route 471: 'There were no traffic jams, but there was alert traffic. There were drivers who increased speed to reach their destination, and it was frightening. Others stopped on the side of the road and got out of the car, dressed in holiday clothes.'

Kibbutz residents hosted 35 residents from northern settlements (Metula, Dan, Snir, Manara, Beit Hillel) for Seder night and three days, providing full board, meals, activities for children, and gifts

Kibbutz member Azulai: 'It's not just Seder night. We are hosting them from the day before the holiday until Saturday. We organized everything we could to give them a good feeling. We set up the accommodation complex for three quiet and safer nights than those they came from.'

Local authority worker: 'And to think that I am hosting my family and my wife's families tonight. There is still an hour until the holiday and we are here in the field, don't know what will happen but if it continues like this they will do the holiday without me.'

Resident: 'We barely prepared anything because we were supposed to be hosted, but who has the courage and desire to leave the house and travel to another city? We have small children and encountering a siren in the middle of the road is not what we are hoping for. If the sirens continue we will stay home.'

Petah Tikva resident: 'It's just amazing. 20 minutes after our neighborhood was in fear due to intense explosions and damage to our homes, within seconds everything flips and everyone returns life to routine as if nothing happened. Suddenly you see everyone going out to walking paths and it doesn't make sense, what kind of people are we who go from fear to hope in a short time.'
Residents of Petah Tikva quickly returned to normal routines and outdoor activities within minutes after missile impact, demonstrating rapid psychological recovery
27-year-old shot and killed in Rahat; third murder in the Arab community within one week
20-year-old man injured in serious and unstable condition with penetrating injury from violence in Taybeh

Survey by 'Oti' autism association of 168 parents: 55% report worsening of their children's condition since Operation 'Lion's Roar' - manifested in bedwetting, rage attacks, violence, lack of treatments, anxiety and clinging to parents
Survey: 57% report significant difficulties since October 7; 70% forced to change work scope or nature; 34% considered moving
Damage to kindergarten building and vehicles in three locations in Nahariya from rocket impacts; no casualties reported
Three people injured in violence incident in Sulam Zohrim: two men aged 23 and 53 injured moderately, one injured lightly with penetrating injuries
Magen David Adom: 68 people treated - 35 physical injuries and 33 anxiety casualties; 12 injured lightly from missile fire; 23 injured on way to safe rooms

Since start of Operation 'Lion's Roar': Magen David Adom treated 2,223 people - 1,745 physical injuries and 478 anxiety casualties; 547 injured from missile fire; 1,198 injured on way to safe rooms; 3 killed; 26 killed in traffic accidents when stopping on roadside during sirens
Two-year-old child felt ill during El Al flight IZ597 from Tel Aviv to Bangkok; emergency landing in Addis Ababa for medical treatment
Major cinema chains Planet and Cinema City announced reopening from end of week despite no change in Home Front Command guidelines

Ministry of Health expanded medical response in Kiryat Shmona, operating 24/7 emergency and trauma care with specialist orthopedic/emergency physician, X-ray services, operating room, wound treatment, infection prevention, casting, and psychological support

Deputy Commander of Zabulon Station, Deputy Sergeant Shmoulik Franco: 'This is one location that suffered a hit and caused significant damage to the kindergarten and even to the apartment building opposite. Fire fighters are conducting searches in apartments and the kindergarten. At the location one person with anxiety is being treated by medical personnel.'

Nesia, 11-year-old from Bnei Brak, injured severely from direct missile hit on Seder night; underwent complex surgery at Sheba Medical Center; remains intubated and sedated in pediatric ICU; younger brother injured moderately
Family held Seder night celebration near daughter's hospital bed with help from local charity organization; community continues public prayers for her recovery
Lucy Aharish: 'It was clear to me that Arabs would pay a price to the State of Israel. We will become more hated and more unaccepted'
Lucy Aharish: 'A pathetic bunch of cowards, total lack of leadership'
National Insurance Institute accelerated unemployment benefit payments to April instead of May; approved ~30,000 applications in a short period from ~50,000 new requests

Environment Ministry issued clear guidance: sensitive populations (heart/lung patients, elderly, children, pregnant women) should avoid strenuous outdoor activity; general population should reduce such activity
Energy Ministry announced resumption of Leviathan gas platform operations after ~5-week shutdown; Karish remains closed; Tamar continues normal operation
2-year-old child became ill during Arkia flight IZ597; emergency landing in Addis Ababa required immediate medical care
11-year-old girl Nesia from Bnei Brak injured by missile shrapnel; in critical condition at Sheba Hospital; underwent surgery during Passover holiday
Bus full of passengers (mothers with children, infants in strollers, fathers with matzah boxes) responded to early warning sirens; passengers recited prayers and Psalms while sheltering

Football team manager Chagai: traveling to Tzfat requires 30-minute drive through area with only 30-second warning time; 'not logical to expect a bus to stop, players to get out and lie down in 30 seconds'
Chagai: league decision to require match in Tzfat is 'disconnected from reality, does not account for real fear of people'; team faces technical loss and heavy fine if they don't travel

Athlete Shir Gavzeh: 'I see the mission as a big but possible challenge. Chances to advance exist completely if we maintain focus and fight for each other and for our country. We definitely have a chance to make history'
Gavzeh: 'We are professionals and know how to adapt ourselves, and especially to prove that we can' despite sacrificing holiday time with families and making many sacrifices
Two 7-month-old infants lightly injured by shrapnel from Iranian ballistic missile strikes in Bnei Brak; 11 impact sites identified in center and north
Over 150 rockets and UAVs fired at north by Hezbollah during Passover; several people lightly injured in Kiryat Shmona and Baana; kindergarten in Nahariya damaged
Iran fired ~10 ballistic missiles during Passover; several people lightly injured in Bnei Brak including two infants
Defense Minister Israel Katz held situation assessment with Chief of Staff, intelligence heads, and senior security officials; issued direct threat to Hezbollah leader Qassem
11 impact sites from Iranian and Lebanese missile fire in center and north; 4 people lightly injured in Bnei Brak including 2 infants
Energy Ministry approved resumption of Leviathan gas platform after 5-week war shutdown; Karish remains closed; Tamar continues operation

Clalit data: 120% increase in psychological support center visits; 36% decrease in lab tests; 12% decrease in adult ER visits, 30% decrease in pediatric ER visits; 10% decrease in medication consumption
Clalit data: elderly and others avoiding medical follow-up for chronic conditions due to fear of leaving homes; ignoring symptoms like chest pain and shortness of breath
Red Crescent/Magen David Adom: 68 people treated in past 24 hours (35 physical injuries, 33 panic cases); 19 killed since Operation Roaring Lion began
Parents of autistic children report catastrophic deterioration in children's condition due to war: disruption of educational routines, sirens, shelter descents

Magen David Adom: 12-year-old and two 7-month-olds lightly injured by shattered glass from Iranian missile strike in Bnei Brak; 24-year-old also lightly injured; 11-year-old girl in critical condition from shrapnel

Environment and Health Ministries issued clear guidance: sensitive populations (heart/lung patients, elderly, children, pregnant women) should avoid strenuous outdoor activity; dust expected to clear by evening
Flower shop owner Ben Cnaan: shop windows shattered March 9, unable to access inventory due to police closure; no income but expenses continue (rent, payments, commitments)
Online fundraiser for flower shop raised NIS 45,000 (~$14,000) to cover repair costs; community members urged to purchase bouquets or donate to sustain 17-year-old business

Church of the Holy Sepulcher closed to public during Holy Week due to Iran war; limited prayer framework approved for clergy and staff only; Cardinal Pizzaballa led Holy Thursday prayers without public attendance

Hezbollah fired ~80 rockets at northern Israel on Passover morning; 2 people lightly injured (34-year-old and 85-year-old) in Kiryat Shmona; property damage including McDonald's near Kibbutz Ma'ayan Baruch
Hundreds of thousands of Israelis forced into shelters during Passover Seder meals on first day of holiday due to Hezbollah rocket barrage

Parents of Nahal Brigade Reconnaissance Unit soldiers sent letter to PM Netanyahu and Defense Minister Katz criticizing 'extremely unreasonable' circumstances: heavy losses, lack of air support, soldiers fighting 3 years on all fronts
Two soldiers of Nahal Brigade Reconnaissance Unit lightly injured in close-range firefight with Hezbollah operative in southern Lebanon; operative killed; weapons cache located
Environmental Protection Ministry recommended sensitive populations (heart/lung patients, elderly, children, pregnant women) avoid strenuous outdoor activity; pollution expected to drop by evening
Church of the Holy Sepulcher limited to clergy and staff for Holy Week due to Iran war; Cardinal Pizzaballa led Holy Thursday prayers without public; rest of Easter celebrations limited

Magen David Adom: two 7-month-old infants lightly wounded by shrapnel from Iranian ballistic missile in Bnei Brak; two men (85 and 34 years old) moderately injured by Hezbollah shrapnel in northern Israel

Mazor pharmacy in Jerusalem's German Colony accepted return of unopened medical supplies after customer's mother died; decided to sell items and use proceeds for charitable purposes rather than refund

Psychotherapist reports clients experiencing 'continuous traumatic stress': children home from school, parents unable to work, businesses collapsing, families stretched with loved ones on reserve duty in North
Over 4 weeks into Operation Roaring Lion, Israelis are adapting, supporting one another, and proving resilience is its own form of victory; life settled into tense but determined rhythm
Sirens activated in Kiryat Shmona and surrounding communities; 2 people lightly wounded (85-year-old and 34-year-old); 6 properties damaged; gas cylinders damaged by shrapnel shut off to prevent fire
Lebanese Health Ministry: 27 killed and 105 wounded in Israeli attacks in past 24 hours; 1,345 total killed since war began; power outages in southern Lebanon regions
Freed hostage's mother: 'I demand to send a humanitarian truck of matzah to him and other hostages before Passover; I appeal to Muslim religious leaders to ensure matzah reaches them'
Ayelet Levy, mother of freed hostage Naama: 'The past has not really passed. Everything that happened to us really happened. Sometimes I have to remind myself that it happened'
An apparent impact was reported in Beit Shemesh, likely caused by debris from an interception.
At least one missile fell in Petah Tikva. Two men injured by shrapnel after a strike near a school in Karmiel area.
MDA medic Mohammad Hussein: 'We treated people suffering from anxiety who were at the scene.'
Deputy Fire Chief Shmulik Franco: 'One person suffering from anxiety is being treated at the scene by medical teams.'
Fire and Rescue forces operating at kindergarten in Nahariya with direct hit causing extensive damage to kindergarten and nearby residential building.
Two IDF soldiers lightly injured during targeted ground operation in southern Lebanon and evacuated to hospital.
Major cinema chains Cinema City and Yes Planet reopening with start of Passover, in accordance with Home Front Command guidelines limiting audiences to 50 per hall.

Education Minister Yoav Kisch: 'An extremist and delusional group of criminals attempted to break into his home under cover of sirens, with protesters choosing to act with provocation and violence instead of evacuating to shelter.'
Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir conducted Passover Seder with 146th brigade at front lines during wartime.

Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir: 'The people of Israel are gathering for the holiday meal, aware that we are at war. We do not return to those days of bondage. We remain, and will continue to strive to be, a people of freedom.'

11-year-old Nesiya from Bnei Brak critically injured in direct hit by Iranian missile; underwent complex surgery at Sheba Tel Hashomer Medical Center. Younger brother moderately injured in same attack.
Local charity organization assisted family in holding Passover Seder meal near hospital ward where injured girl is hospitalized.
Community in Bnei Brak holding public prayers for Nesiya's full recovery.
